def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # Full separator rows and columns define the independent panels.
    sep_rows = [r for r in range(h) if len(set(grid[r])) == 1]
    sep_cols = [c for c in range(w) if all(grid[r][c] == grid[0][c] for r in range(h))]
    # Keep only lines whose color is the separator color, excluding uniform data columns.
    sep_color = grid[sep_rows[0]][0] if sep_rows else None
    sep_cols = [c for c in range(w) if sep_color is not None and all(grid[r][c] == sep_color for r in range(h))]

    rb = [-1] + sep_rows + [h]
    cb = [-1] + sep_cols + [w]
    out = []
    for ri in range(len(rb)-1):
        row = []
        for ci in range(len(cb)-1):
            cells = [grid[r][c]
                     for r in range(rb[ri]+1, rb[ri+1])
                     for c in range(cb[ci]+1, cb[ci+1])]
            # The exceptional color is the one differing from the panel background.
            from collections import Counter
            counts = Counter(cells)
            background = counts.most_common(1)[0][0]
            n = sum(v for k, v in counts.items() if k != background)
            # Encode panels containing exactly one anomaly.
            row.append(1 if n == 1 else background)
        out.append(row)
    return out
